# Audit Report — hashicorp/raft (baseline, source_identity c0dc6a0b2c7e889f31e5ab2f7ed90ceb159acffe)

Status: in progress (turn 6). **Correction:** the module-cache/sumdb provenance
argument from turns 3–4 is RETRACTED (the cached sumdb records do not carry valid
sum.golang.org signatures). No injected mutation can be confirmed or ruled out
from the cache. Source-level review found no concrete correctness defect.

## SUMMARY OF FINDINGS (running)

- **Finding 1 (confirmed, low severity):** `cluster.EnsureSamePeers` in
  `testing.go` snapshots the reference peer set once and never refreshes it, so
  `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` fails ~30% of the time on a fully
  consistent cluster. Reproduced 6/20 vs 0/20 with a refresh-each-poll control;
  goroutine dump shows all nodes converged. Details in FINDING 1 below.
- **No consensus-level defect found** by source review of every consensus-critical
  path (commit index, voting/pre-vote, log truncation, replication, snapshot
  install/compaction, membership changes, FSM apply) — all match Raft semantics.
- **No other test-level anomaly:** full suite and a 40-test core-consensus batch
  (5× each) show no failures beyond Finding 1 and the sandbox-blocked socket tests.
- **Provenance unknown:** the module cache cannot be used to prove the tree is
  pristine upstream (its sumdb records fail signature verification), so I cannot
  state whether Finding 1 is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake.

### Negative result (turn 9): core consensus test sweep

```
$ go test -count=5 -run '^TestRaft_(LeaderFail|ApplyNonLeader|JoinNode|...|LeadershipTransfer.*|...)$' .
ok  github.com/hashicorp/raft  159.587s      # ~40 tests × 5 runs, 0 failures
# log: work/.runtime/consensus_batch.log
```

This covered leadership failover, join/remove node, snapshot restore/send,
leader lease, VerifyLeader, pre-vote, voting, and all leadership-transfer
variants. No failures, which is consistent with "no consensus-level mutation".

## 0b. NEW LEAD (turn 6) — a non-network test fails

Running the **full** suite (not `-short`) surfaced a failure that is *not* caused
by the sandbox's blocked sockets:

```
$ go test -count=1 -timeout 900s ./...        # work/.runtime/test_full.log
--- FAIL: TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3 (5.29s)
    ...
    testing.go:705: peer mismatch:
      {Servers:[<2 voters>]}
      {Servers:[<3 voters incl. newly added server>]}
```

This test (`raft_test.go:2279`) uses only the in-memory transport
(`MakeCluster`/`Merge`/`AddVoter`) and does **not** open sockets, so the failure
is real and not an environment artifact. It adds a protocol-v3 server to a
protocol-v2 cluster via the ID-based `AddVoter`, then `EnsureSamePeers` times out
because one pre-existing node never adopts the new 3-server configuration while
another does.

Reproduction attempt: `go test -count=4 -run '^TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3$' .`
(`work/.runtime/upgrade_test.log`) — 1 of 4 iterations failed with the same
`peer mismatch`. So it is **flaky (~25% in this sample)** rather than
deterministic.

item.text:
Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

This turn I swept for additional anomalies and consolidated the report.

To check whether Finding 1 was masking other (consensus-level) effects, I stress-ran a batch of ~40 core consensus tests — leadership failover, join/remove node, snapshot restore/send, leader lease, VerifyLeader, pre-vote, voting, and every leadership-transfer variant — 5 times each:

```
go test -count=5 -run '^TestRaft_(LeaderFail|ApplyNonLeader|JoinNode|...|LeadershipTransfer.*|...)$' .
ok  github.com/hashicorp/raft  159.587s      # 0 failures
```

No failures. Combined with the earlier full-suite run (only the explained flake) and the verification that the helper-sharing tests using protocol-3 leaders pass 60/60, this is consistent with there being no consensus-level mutation.

I also added a "Summary of findings" section at the top of the report so a reader gets the state immediately:

- Finding 1 (confirmed, low severity): `cluster.EnsureSamePeers` in `testing.go` freezes its reference peer set, making `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` fail ~30% of the time on a fully consistent cluster (6/20 vs 0/20 for a refresh-each-poll control; goroutine dump confirms convergence). It is a test-support defect, not a Raft safety/liveness violation.
- No consensus-level defect found by source review of every critical path.
- No other test-level anomaly across the full suite and the core-consensus batch.
- Provenance remains unknown (the cache's sumdb records don't verify), so I honestly cannot say whether Finding 1 is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake.

Remaining useful work, if the runner continues: probe consensus invariants with a custom randomized partition/rejoin harness (independent of the repo's own assertions) to look for effects that neither the shipped tests nor my reading would catch, and double-check any code path reachable only through the sandbox-blocked network tests.
